metaDescription: Six hedge trimmers under $50, from corded 16 and 17 inch units to cordless 2-in-1 shears, compared on cut capacity, weight and what the cap really buys.
expertTake: The Black+Decker 17 inch corded trimmer is the best pick under $50 for real hedges, and the 16 inch corded unit is the cheaper alternative. The Supleap and OGERY cordless shears are the value picks for borders and small shrubs. If your hedge has stems thicker than a pencil, no trimmer at this cap will cope and you need loppers.
introParagraphs: A tight cap forces a real choice between two very different tools. Plug-in trimmers give you a full-length blade and unlimited runtime, while cheap battery shears give you freedom but a small blade and a small battery.

Neither route buys power. At this level the useful questions are how thick a stem the blade gap will take, how heavy the tool feels over ten minutes, and whether you can live with a cord. This guide sorts the options on those points.

products.name: Black+Decker 17 in. Corded Hedge Trimmer, 3.2 Amp, Dual Action
products.description:
This is the tool most gardens under the cap should buy. A 17 inch hardened steel dual-action blade is long enough to cover a hedge top quickly, and the 3.2 amp motor is rated to cut stems up to 5/8 inch thick. Dual-action blades cut on both strokes, which reduces vibration compared with single-action designs.

The real advantage is that a cord removes the battery question. You never run out of charge, there is no pack to age, and the weight sits in the tool rather than in a lithium cell, which makes it light and balanced for a plug-in. The cost is the cord, which limits your reach to the length of an extension and demands care so you do not cut it.

It will not take thick stems, and trying to do so will stall it. Keep the cord behind you, use a rated outdoor extension and wipe resin off the blade after each session. Next to the 16 inch sibling, it offers a longer blade for slightly more weight, and for most hedges that is the better trade. It is a plain, durable tool that costs little to keep. If you hedge twice a year, this style of tool can last a decade because it has no battery to degrade and few parts to fail.
products.bestFor: Hedges within reach of an outlet and extension cord.
pros: Unlimited runtime with no battery to age
cons: Cord limits reach and needs care
Will stall on stems thicker than 5/8 in.

products.name: Black+Decker BEHT100 16 in. Corded Hedge Trimmer, 3.0 Amp
products.description:
The BEHT100 is the smaller, simpler corded option. A 16 inch blade is a little shorter than its 17 inch sibling and a 3.0 amp motor is a little weaker, but the listed capacity is the same 5/8 inch, so it handles the same kind of growth at a slightly slower pace.

What sets it apart is the cord retention system, a clip that holds the extension cord in place at the handle so that a tug does not unplug it mid-cut. That sounds small, but pulled plugs and cut cords are the commonest annoyance with corded trimmers, and this feature addresses both.

The compact body makes it easy to store, and it is the more manageable choice for a small garden. Wipe the blade after use, store it with the guard on and inspect the cord for nicks before each session. If your hedge is longer than about ten metres, the 17 inch unit will save you time. Because both Black+Decker trimmers use the same dual-action idea, the choice between them comes down to length against weight, not to any difference in how they cut. Many owners keep the compact one for tight corners and tidy edges near walls.
products.bestFor: Small gardens and users who want a compact, simple corded tool.
pros: Cord retention clip stops accidental unplugging
Compact body is easy to store
Same 5/8 in. capacity as the 17 inch

products.name: Supleap 21V 600W 2-in-1 Cordless Hedge Trimmer and Grass Shear
products.description:
Supleap sells this as a cordless 2-in-1 with a battery level display, a head that adjusts to several angles and double-sided blades. The 600W label describes a peak input figure, not a continuous cutting power, so treat it as a marketing number rather than a measure of capability.

The tool is lightweight with an anti-slip grip, which is the real appeal: you can carry it to a border, trim a few shrubs and put it down without dragging a cord across the lawn. The blade is short, so this is a trimmer for tidy shrubs, not for a long boundary hedge.

What you give up against the corded Black+Decker is capacity and runtime: a small battery will run flat in a session and the cutting width is far smaller. Keep it charged, wipe the blades after use and store the battery away from cold sheds. For under the cap it is a sensible tool for light work. The battery display is worth using, since a small pack that dies mid-cut leaves you with a half-trimmed shrub. Charge it fully before a session and stop when the display drops to the last bar.
products.bestFor: Border shrubs and edging where a cord would be a nuisance.
pros: Multi-angle head for edging and shrubs
cons: 600W is a marketing figure, not a cutting spec

products.name: Ogery 21V Cordless Hedge Trimmer and Grass Shear, 8.9 in., Two 1500mAh Batteries
products.description:
Two batteries in the box is what sets this kit apart in the budget class. Two 21V 1500mAh packs mean you can swap and keep going, and the 8.9 inch hedge blade and grass shear are interchangeable on one body.

The motor is rated up to 2,000 RPM, a no-load figure, and the blade is small, so it is best used on soft growth such as boxwood or lavender. It is not a replacement for a corded 17 inch trimmer on a long hedge, but it is easier to carry and has no cable.

The small cells charge quickly, but they also drain quickly, so plan on working in short bursts. Keep the blades clean, avoid forcing it into thick stems and store the batteries partly charged. It is the best pick here for anyone who wants cordless freedom and a spare pack. Against the Supleap, it gives up the battery display but gains the second pack, which matters more when you are working a whole border. Rotate the two packs so neither sits flat for months.
products.bestFor: Soft shrubs and borders where two batteries matter.
pros: Hedge blade and grass shear on one body
cons: 8.9 in. blade is too small for long hedges

products.name: Cordless 2-in-1 Shrub Trimmer and Grass Shear, 9 in. Hedge Blade, 3 Angles
products.description:
This model pairs a 9 inch hedge blade with a 5.3 inch grass shear and an adjustable head that locks at 15, 30 and 45 degrees. The angle range is its strength, because it lets you hold the body comfortably while the blade lies flat or tilted, which helps on topiary and low borders.

The motor is listed at 1,500 RPM with no load, which is lower than the OGERY, and the dual-action blade gives cleaner cuts on soft growth than a single-action design. Like the other shears it is aimed at shaping, not at cutting thick stems.

The seller is not a major brand, so check the warranty and spare-battery availability before buying. Wipe the blade clean after each use and store the battery partly charged. If you mostly need to edge lawn borders and tidy small shrubs, it does that at a very low cost. Use the lowest head angle for edging so the blade sits flat to the ground, and keep your free hand clear of the blade path. The adjustable head reduces wrist bend, which is the main reason to prefer it to a fixed-head shear.
products.bestFor: Topiary, low borders and small shrubs needing angle control.
cons: Lower no-load speed than some rivals

products.name: Dekopro 8V Cordless Grass Shear and Handheld Hedge Trimmer, 1.5 lb
products.description:
At 1.5 pounds this is the lightest tool in the guide, and the head tilts from +45 to -60 degrees, a wide range that makes it easy to cut at awkward angles. A start key at the base of the handle prevents accidental startup, a safety feature that is more thoughtful than it sounds on a tool this small.

The 8V battery is the smallest here, so this is a shear for tidying, not for cutting back growth. If you need a quick tool to clip a few stems or edge a patch of lawn, it is the one to reach for.

It will not replace a hedge trimmer on a hedge, and it stands as the budget option for light, quick jobs. Keep the blades clean, charge the battery before use and store the tool dry. For the cap, it is the cheapest route to a battery-powered shear. Because its 8V pack is tiny, recharge it after every use rather than waiting for it to die, which keeps the cell healthier. It is a good second tool to keep in a drawer next to a full-size trimmer.
products.bestFor: Quick tidying jobs and edging where weight must be minimal.
pros: 1.5 lb is the lightest tool here
cons: Not a replacement for a full trimmer

buyingCriteria.explanation: The two Black+Decker trimmers are corded and give unlimited runtime with a 16 to 17 inch blade. The Supleap, Ogery, 9 inch shear and Dekopro are cordless shears with blades of 9 inches or less. At this cap, corded buys cutting width and cordless buys convenience.
The two corded trimmers are listed at 5/8 inch. The cordless shears do not list a thickness figure, so assume they cut green stems no thicker than a pencil. Anything thicker needs a lopper.
A 17 inch blade covers a top far faster than a 9 inch blade. The corded Black+Decker 17 inch is the best option for any hedge longer than a few metres. Shears are for details.

Corded trimmers weigh more than shears, but the cord adds no weight at the tool. The Dekopro at 1.5 pounds is the lightest here. Over ten minutes a lighter tool saves your wrists, even if it cuts less.
A cord is a cutting hazard. The BEHT100 has a cord retention clip that stops accidental unplugging. Always route the cord behind you and use an outdoor-rated extension.

The cap reflects listing prices when this guide was updated, and prices move. Under $50 you are choosing between a full-size corded tool and a small cordless shear, never a full-size cordless trimmer with a strong battery.

howWeEvaluated.title: Cutting fit
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared blade length and listed capacity. The 17 inch corded unit led. Shears scored lower for hedge work but well for borders.

howWeEvaluated.title: Under-cap check
howWeEvaluated.description: We kept only items whose live listing price was at or below the cap when the guide was updated. Prices move, so recheck before buying.

howWeEvaluated.title: Weight and comfort
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared listed weights. The 1.5 lb Dekopro scored highest, and the corded units scored well for balance.

howWeEvaluated.title: Battery and cord handling
howWeEvaluated.description: We looked at the number of batteries and cord management. The Ogery's two batteries and the BEHT100's cord clip scored well.

howWeEvaluated.title: Ownership
howWeEvaluated.description: We considered blade care, cord inspection and battery storage. Major brands scored higher for support.

cards.label: Corded
cards.text: The two Black+Decker trimmers give full-size blades and unlimited runtime. You need an outlet and must manage the cord.

cards.label: Cordless
cards.text: The Supleap, Ogery, 9 inch shear and Dekopro are portable and cord-free, but small. They suit borders and shrubs.

howToChoose.note: Pick corded for a real hedge and cordless for tidy borders.

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: Look for a short blade, light weight and either a short cord or a swappable battery. A small garden rarely needs a long blade.

cards.label: In this comparison
cards.text: The Black+Decker BEHT100 16 inch suits a small garden near an outlet, and the Ogery with two batteries suits one without a convenient socket.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: Spend more if your hedge is long or thick. At the top of this cap, only the 17 inch corded unit cuts to 5/8 inch, and beyond the cap you get cordless kits with larger batteries.

cards.label: Save if
cards.text: Save if you only edge borders. The Dekopro or the 9 inch shear are the cheapest and lightest ways to do that.

maintenance.why: Sap and moisture build up on the teeth. A light oil coat prevents rust.
Nicks and cuts expose wire. Replace a damaged cord before use.
Store them partly charged and away from frost. Small cells age quickly if left flat.
A bent guard bar causes stalling. Straighten or replace it.
The cover protects both blade and hands. Always fit it.

faq.q: Is a corded or cordless trimmer better under $50?
faq.a: For a real hedge, corded wins because it gives a 16 to 17 inch blade and unlimited runtime. For borders and small shrubs, a cordless shear is easier to carry.

The corded Black+Decker trimmers are listed to 5/8 inch. The cordless shears do not list a figure, so assume pencil thickness and use loppers for more. Check the current listing before you buy, since a stated capacity on a seller's page is sometimes generous. Pushing a small blade into thick wood is the quickest way to burn out a cheap motor.
It is a label for a small battery tool, so treat it as marketing. A more useful measure is blade length and the battery's capacity.
Yes. The $50 cap reflects listing prices when this guide was updated, so check the current price before you buy.

faq.q: How long do small batteries last?
faq.a: Expect short runs, often under half an hour, from 1500mAh or 8V packs. Plan to work in bursts and charge between sessions, and consider that a spare battery is often the most useful extra you can buy.

faq.q: Can I cut a thick hedge with these?
faq.a: No. Thick or woody hedges need a stronger cordless trimmer or a gas machine, which cost more than this cap. If your hedge is overgrown, cut it back by hand with loppers first and then use a trimmer for the regular maintenance cuts. That two-step approach keeps a cheap tool from being overloaded.
